questions.question: Which design needs a paired t-test?
options: Test scores of two different classes
Each of 20 patients' blood pressure before and after a drug
Treatment versus control with different people
questions.explanation: Measuring the same people twice creates natural pairs. The other designs compare different people, which is the independent two-sample case.

questions.question: A paired t-test is equivalent to a one-sample t-test on...
questions.explanation: You compute each pair's difference and test whether the mean difference is 0.

questions.question: Eight pairs have differences 7, 4, 7, 3, 8, 9, 3, 8 (mean 6.125, SD 2.416). What is t?
How many degrees of freedom does the paired t-test above have?
questions.explanation: df = n − 1 where n is the number of pairs (8), so df = 7.

questions.question: Why does the independent test miss an effect that the paired test finds?
options: The large differences between people inflate its standard error
questions.explanation: Between-person variation is part of the independent SE. In a paired design each person acts as their own control, so that variation cancels out of the differences.

questions.question: 20 students' scores before and after a review session rise by 6.2 points on average. Why can't the paired test alone prove the review caused the gain?
options: There is no control group: practice or familiarity could explain the improvement
questions.explanation: Statistics can show that scores changed. Establishing the cause needs a design with a comparison (control) group.
